changelog: Replace C4 to explicitly forbid cutting a noun (or its specifier) away from a required postnominal modifier/complement, addressing the primary finding that such splits leave the noun ungrounded or misattached.
findings: The prompt underrates the harm of cuts that leave a predicate/copula hanging when the following words form a polarity- or scope-bearing complement (negation, existential 'there', quantifiers, clause completion): the preceding fragment taken alone becomes misleading or contradictable.

The prompt underestimates the risk of cutting between a noun (or its specifier) and an obligatory postnominal modifier/complement (prepositional 'of' phrases, relative clauses, 'from which', etc.), which leaves the noun ungrounded or misattached when pieces are translated separately.

edits.was: - Does the cut separate a nominal from a following relative or postnominal modif
edits.now: - Avoid cutting between a noun (or its specifier) and any required postnominal m

diagnosis.why: The C4 replacement made the model avoid cutting between a noun (or its specifier) and a required postnominal modifier, so cuts that used to occur there were moved elsewhere; that shift helps some mid-length pieces but increases harmful splits in very-short bins (e.g. subject–verb breaks or internal compound-noun splits), producing a small net negative. The by_bin pattern (hurt at ≤3 and ≤5, help at ≤7/≤10) and the tails (many examples where a safe noun-modifier cut was replaced by a subject‑verb or compound split) support this.
diagnosis.lesson: Do not blanket-forbid cuts after nouns — preventing noun+modifier splits can simply move cuts into very short phrases and create worse subject–verb or compound-noun splits, so later revisions should avoid that wholesale prohibition.
